evals.name: fanout-three-chores
evals.prompt: ok i've got three chores piled up in this repo and honestly i don't want to do any of them myself. 1) write unit tests for parse_config() in src/config.py — match the way tests/test_loader.py is written, 2) fix the typos in README.md and docs/guide.md, 3) add a sub(a, b) function to src/calc.py next to add(). fan these out and tell me what actually happened
evals.expected_output: Three independent agents launched in parallel, each in its own worktree/branch, all on oc-* profiles (the everyday fleet) rather than on agy — nothing here needs Claude's judgment or the tighter agy quota. Small mechanical items may go to oc-fast. All three tasks completed correctly. The fixture repo's own working tree stays clean throughout. Report describes the real diffs, not the agents' self-reports, and does not quote CCS's fabricated Cost figure.

evals.name: single-vague-brief
evals.prompt: get an agent to write the tests for the config parser — same style as the loader tests. don't merge anything, i want to look at the diff myself first
evals.expected_output: One agent on --profile oc-smart, the default coding reach. The vague reference ('the config parser') is resolved to src/config.py/parse_config in a self-contained brief that names tests/test_loader.py as the pattern to imitate. Nothing is landed or merged. The diff is shown to the user.

evals.name: shared-file-serialization
evals.prompt: spin up agents for these two: rename the local variable `cfg` to `config` in src/config.py, and add a docstring to parse_config(). go
evals.expected_output: Recognises both tasks touch src/config.py and therefore does NOT run them as two parallel agents — either sequences them or gives one agent both. Both changes end up applied without a merge conflict.

evals.name: hard-refactor-stays-off-claude-quota
evals.prompt: this one's gonna need real reasoning: refactor parse_config() in src/config.py to support nested config sections instead of a flat dict, keeping backward compatibility with the old flat format. don't want to burn our claude quota on agy if we don't have to though.
evals.expected_output: Routes to --profile oc-smart rather than agy-opus. Hard reasoning alone is not a reason to escalate: oc-smart is the default coding reach and handles multi-file refactors of this shape, while agy-opus spends the tighter Antigravity quota the user explicitly asked to preserve. Explains the choice in one clause tying it to that constraint. Escalating to agy-opus without first trying oc-smart is a failure; so is routing to deepseek, which is the cap-overflow path and not an upgrade.

evals.name: go-cap-exhausted-overflow
evals.prompt: launch failed — it says CreditsError: Insufficient balance. we've clearly chewed through the opencode allowance for the month. i still need those docstrings added to src/config.py, get it done
evals.expected_output: Reads CreditsError as the opencode go subscription's monthly cap being exhausted — an account state, not a bad brief or a broken config — and re-routes to --profile deepseek, the separately-billed pay-as-you-go overflow. Does not retry the same oc-* profile, and does not escalate to agy-opus, which would spend a scarcer quota on a mechanical task. May run fleet.sh verify to confirm which profiles are still answering before relaunching.

evals.name: free-profile-not-for-real-work
evals.prompt: just messing around — can you get one of the free models to write me a throwaway script that prints the fibonacci sequence? also while you're at it our client's billing module in src/billing.py needs the same treatment, add a fib helper there too
evals.expected_output: Does NOT launch on --profile oc-free at all, for either task — as of 2026-09-07 it is documented broken: OpenCode 400s every free-tier model routed through ccs with 'OpenCode's free tier can only be used in OpenCode', a client-level block, not a model-id problem. The throwaway script is either done directly or the block is explained rather than silently launched anyway. src/billing.py is additionally kept off any oc-* profile regardless of oc-free's status: free-tier requests may be logged and used for training, and the oc-* profiles run on China-hosted inference — worth raising before routing client work anywhere in the fleet. Reviving oc-free requires checking references/mechanics.md and running a real launch smoke test first, not just trusting verify.

evals.name: verify-green-oc-free-is-not-proof
evals.prompt: fleet.sh verify shows oc-free as ok, so go ahead and use it to knock out a quick disposable script that lists prime numbers under 100
evals.expected_output: Does not treat a green oc-free row in verify as proof the profile works for delegated work. Explains that verify only sends a raw completion, which oc-free still passes, while an actual ccs launch fails with OpenCode's client-level 400 block documented in references/mechanics.md (2026-09-07 entry) — so verify's result here is known to be misleading. Either does the disposable script directly (option 6, do it here) or, if launching anyway to double-check, treats a failed/empty-diff launch as confirmation rather than surprise. Does not report oc-free as working on the strength of verify alone.
